insight: 매출 목표는 단계별 전환율의 곱이다. 맨 위에 손님을 더 붓기 전에 가장 크게 새는 단계를 먼저 고치면 같은 결과를 더 싸게 얻는다.
misconception: 판매를 늘리려면 문의나 리드를 더 많이 모으는 것이 먼저다.

cards.title: Why 100 inquiries became only 10 bookings
body: A restaurant gets about 100 private-event inquiries a month. Birthdays, team dinners, small weddings.
Only 10 turn into booked events. The owner wants 15. The obvious fix is more inquiries. The numbers point somewhere cheaper.

image.label: A funnel of event inquiries narrowing to a few bookings
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 위쪽에 이메일·전화 아이콘 100개가 쏟아져 들어가는 깔때기, 아래로 갈수록 좁아지고 맨 아래에는 예약 확정 카드 10장. 깔때기 윗부분 옆면에 구멍이 나 아이콘이 많이 새어 나가는 모습. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: You want 15 events a month, not 10.
body: Of 100 inquiries, 25 come in for a tasting or visit. Of those, 20 ask for a proposal. Half of those book.

options.text: Spend more on ads to get 150 inquiries
options.feedback: The math works: 150 inquiries at the same rates gives 15 events. But you pay for 50% more leads while 75 of every 100 still slip away.

options.text: Find out why 75 of 100 inquiries never come in for a tasting
options.feedback: That's the biggest leak. Fixing it uses inquiries you already paid for. Next card shows how small a change is enough.

options.text: Offer a discount so more proposals turn into bookings
options.feedback: You'd need 75% of proposals to book instead of 50%, and every event would earn less. You'd be fixing the stage that already works best.

cards.title: Follow 100 inquiries.
body: Overall, 10 in 100 book. Now raise only the first step, from 25 to about 38 tastings. The rest stays the same: 38 × 80% × 50% ≈ **15 events**. Same result as 50% more inquiries.

breakdown.label: Tastings
breakdown.detail: Only 25% come in. 75 are lost here

breakdown.label: Proposals
breakdown.detail: 80% of tastings ask for a quote

cards.title: The pipeline
body: A **pipeline** is the path a customer takes from first contact to paying, split into stages. Each stage has a **conversion rate**: the share who move on to the next one.
Sales are those rates multiplied together. That means improving any stage lifts the final number just as much as filling the top. You also see exactly where customers leave.

image.label: Four connected stages with a percentage on each link
image.brief: 가로로 이어진 파이프 네 칸: "Inquiry", "Tasting", "Proposal", "Booking". 칸 사이 연결부에 "25%", "80%", "50%" 라벨. 첫 연결부가 가장 가늘고 물이 새는 모습으로 강조.

cards.softwareNote: The same stages appear as sign-up, setup, demo and purchase. Product analytics often shows each rate automatically, so the biggest leak is usually visible in a dashboard.

cards.title: Work backward from your goal.
body: Divide your target by your overall rate. Fifteen events at 10% means 150 inquiries. Now you know what the top of the pipeline must hold.

Add time. If an inquiry takes about six weeks to become a booking, this month's inquiries are next quarter's events. A quiet inbox today shows up as empty tables later. The lag differs by business, so measure your own.

image.label: Calendar showing inquiries today turning into events weeks later
image.brief: 달력 두 장. 왼쪽 이번 달 달력에 문의 아이콘들, 화살표로 6주 뒤 오른쪽 달력의 이벤트 테이블 아이콘으로 이어짐. "~6 weeks" 라벨.

cards.title: The rates are not fixed laws.
body: Push one stage too hard and the next one can drop. If you pressure every inquiry into a tasting, you may get more tastings from people who were never going to book.
Small numbers wobble. Twenty proposals a month can swing from 40% to 60% by chance. Track several months before you act.
Define each stage the same way every time, or the rates mean nothing.

cards.title: Now it's a scheduling app.
body: Each month, 300 people start a free trial. 20% finish setup. Half of those book a call. Half of the calls buy. That's 15 new customers. You want 30.

options.text: Double ad spend to get 600 trials
options.feedback: It gets you to 30, but doubles your cost, and extra users from ads are often less ready to buy than the first 300.

options.text: Help new users finish setup, lifting it from 20% to 40%
options.feedback: Setup is where 80% of users quit, so it has the most room. Doubling that one rate also doubles sales, using trials you already have.

options.text: Offer a big discount on every sales call
options.feedback: To reach 30 this way, every single call would have to buy. You'd cut your price and still fall short.

cards.title: Sales are a chain of rates. Fix the weakest link first.
body: Map your stages, count how many move through each, and work backward from your goal before you buy more leads.
**Try it today:** write down your last month's numbers for each stage, from first contact to paid. Circle the step where the most people drop out.
